I also need to correct one line in my first answer. I wrote that COBIT 2019 has a "successor, COBIT 2019 with updates," which doesn't make sense. COBIT 2019 is the current version, and it replaced COBIT 5. ISACA has released supplementary guidance since, but there's no separate successor framework.

Also, since you're aiming for certification, note that the transition deadline for ISO/IEC 27001:2022 passed in October 2025. Any new certification will be against the 2022 version, which is what the Annex A references in my mapping table use.

When you pick this back up, I can help with a gap-analysis checklist or a Statement of Applicability template.

# Gap Analysis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 for a 250-Person Fintech

Statuses below are **assumptions inferred from your snapshot**, not findings. Validate each with evidence (screenshots, tickets, policies, configs) before you rely on them.

**Status key:** Strong / Partial / Gap / Unknown
**Effort key:** **QW** = quick win (documentation or config, roughly 1 to 6 weeks), **M** = medium (1 to 3 months), **L** = long project (3+ months)

## Part 1: Management system clauses (4-10)

Annex A gets the attention, but missing clauses 4-10 are the most common reason first audits fail. Your PCI and SOX programs probably cover little of this.

| Clause | Requirement | Likely status | Action | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | Context, interested parties, ISMS scope | Gap | Define scope (see note below), list interested parties (regulators, card brands, auditors, customers) | QW |
| 5 | Leadership commitment, policy, roles | Partial | Sign an ISMS policy, name an ISMS owner, record management commitment | QW |
| 6.1.2-6.1.3 | Risk assessment and treatment, SoA | Gap | Choose a methodology, build a risk register, write a treatment plan, produce the SoA | M |
| 6.2 | Security objectives | Gap | Set 4 to 6 measurable objectives (e.g., critical patches within SLA) | QW |
| 7 | Resources, competence, awareness, documented information | Partial | Document control, competence records | QW |
| 8 | Operational planning and risk treatment execution | Partial | Run the treatment plan | M |
| 9.1-9.3 | Monitoring and metrics, **internal audit**, **management review** | Gap | Build an audit program (can borrow SOX internal audit capacity) and hold a first management review | M |
| 10 | Nonconformity and corrective action, continual improvement | Partial | Corrective-action log (your ITIL problem and CSI processes can be adapted) | QW |

**Scoping note:** Your scope decision drives total effort. Options are (a) the whole company, (b) the payment platform and supporting infrastructure, or (c) the full production environment. Most regulated fintechs pick (b) or (c) to align with the PCI CDE and SOX-relevant systems, which lets you reuse existing evidence.

## Part 2: Annex A gap checklist

### Theme 5: Organizational controls (37)

| Controls | Likely status | Gap and action | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.1 Policies; 5.2 Roles; 5.4 Mgmt responsibilities; 5.36 Compliance with policies; 5.37 Documented procedures | Partial | Consolidate PCI and SOX policies into one ISMS policy set, build a RACI, and add an annual review cycle | QW |
| 5.3 Segregation of duties | Partial | Document an SoD matrix, reusing SOX work | QW |
| 5.5 Contact with authorities; 5.6 Special interest groups | Gap | Maintain a contact list (regulators, law enforcement, acquirer, AWS, card brands) and join an industry group such as FS-ISAC | QW |
| 5.7 Threat intelligence | Gap | Subscribe to a few feeds (CISA KEV, AWS and VMware advisories) and add a lightweight triage step | QW |
| 5.8 InfoSec in project management | Partial | Add a security checklist to project and change intake | QW |
| 5.9 Asset inventory | Partial | Complete the CMDB, using AWS Config or discovery for cloud and vCenter exports for on-prem, and assign owners | **M/L** |
| 5.10 Acceptable use; 5.11 Return of assets | Partial | Write the AUP and tie asset return to the offboarding checklist | QW |
| 5.12 Classification; 5.13 Labelling | Gap | Define 3 to 4 levels (include cardholder data), then label gradually | QW / M |
| 5.14 Information transfer | Partial | Transfer policy, approved encrypted channels | QW |
| 5.15 Access control; 5.16 Identity mgmt; 5.17 Authentication info; 5.18 Access rights | Partial | SSO helps. Formalize joiner/mover/leaver, run periodic access reviews (likely already done for SOX), and set a password and secret-handling standard | QW |
| 5.19-5.22 Supplier security, agreements, ICT supply chain, monitoring | Gap/Unknown | Build a supplier inventory, tier by criticality, add security clauses, and review annually. This overlaps PCI 12.8 | M |
| 5.23 Cloud services | Partial | Cloud security policy, shared-responsibility matrix, AWS baseline (CIS benchmark, Security Hub) | QW / M |
| 5.24-5.28 Incident management | Partial | ITIL incident process is a good base. Add a security incident category, severity criteria, an IR plan and playbooks, evidence handling, and a tabletop exercise | QW / M |
| 5.29 Security during disruption; 5.30 ICT continuity readiness | Partial | Backups are tested, but add a BIA, RTO/RPO per system, a DR plan, and a DR test (not just restore tests) | M |
| 5.31 Legal and regulatory requirements | Partial | Build a register (PCI DSS, SOX, GLBA, state laws, GDPR if applicable) | QW |
| 5.32 IP; 5.33 Records protection; 5.34 Privacy | Unknown | Retention schedule, privacy roles, and PII handling | QW / M |
| 5.35 Independent review | Gap | Annual independent review (internal audit or external) | M |

### Theme 6: People controls (8)

| Controls | Likely status | Gap and action | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6.1 Screening; 6.2 Employment terms; 6.4 Disciplinary; 6.5 Post-termination; 6.6 NDAs | Unknown | Confirm with HR: background checks (likely needed for fintech), security clauses in contracts, NDAs | QW |
| 6.3 Awareness and training | Partial | PCI probably requires training already. Add role-based training (developers, admins), phishing simulations, and records | QW |
| 6.7 Remote working | Unknown | Remote-work policy and VPN/ZTNA, device requirements | QW |
| 6.8 Event reporting | Partial | Publish a single channel and a "how to report" guide | QW |

### Theme 7: Physical controls (14)

Applicability depends on whether your VMware environment is in a colocation facility, a company-owned data center, or a closet. **Ask early.**

| Controls | Likely status | Gap and action | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7.1-7.6, 7.8, 7.11-7.13 (perimeters, entry, monitoring, environment, utilities, cabling, maintenance) | Unknown | If colo, collect the provider's SOC 2 or ISO certificate and treat as inherited. If owned, do a physical walkthrough and fill gaps (access logs, CCTV, fire suppression, UPS) | QW (colo) / L (owned) |
| 7.7 Clear desk and screen | Gap | Policy plus screen-lock enforcement | QW |
| 7.9 Off-premises assets; 7.10 Storage media; 7.14 Secure disposal | Partial | Media handling and disposal procedure with certificates of destruction | QW |

### Theme 8: Technological controls (34)

| Controls | Likely status | Gap and action | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8.1 Endpoint devices; 8.7 Malware | Unknown | Verify MDM, disk encryption, and EDR coverage | QW |
| **8.2 Privileged access rights** | **Gap (no PAM)** | **Interim:** separate admin accounts, MFA on all admin access, AWS IAM Identity Center with least-privilege roles, a break-glass procedure, and quarterly privileged-access review. **Target:** PAM tool with vaulting and session recording for on-prem and AWS | QW (interim) / **L** (PAM) |
| 8.3 Access restriction; 8.5 Secure authentication | Partial | Enforce MFA everywhere, especially the CDE (PCI 8.4.2) | QW / M |
| 8.4 Source code access | Unknown | Restrict repo access, branch protection | QW |
| 8.6 Capacity | Partial | ITIL cap

# Annex A Gap Checklist, continued (8.6 to 8.34)

Themes 5, 6, and 7 were completed in the previous section, so Theme 8 is the only part left. The earlier Theme 8 rows covered 8.1 to 8.5 and 8.7 (malware, grouped with 8.1), so this picks up at 8.6.

Statuses are still **assumptions from your snapshot**, so validate each with evidence. PCI references assume PCI DSS v4.0.1, and your QSA's interpretation governs.

**Effort key:** **QW** = quick win (about 1 to 6 weeks), **M** = medium (1 to 3 months), **L** = long project (3+ months)

## Theme 8: Technological controls (8.6 to 8.34)

| Controls | Likely status | Gap and action | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8.6 Capacity management | Partial | ITIL capacity practice likely exists. Add thresholds and alerts (CloudWatch, vCenter) and a periodic capacity review record | QW |
| **8.8 Technical vulnerability management** ⭐ | **Gap** | See priority section below. Quarterly patching alone likely won't satisfy PCI 6.3.3 (critical patches within one month) | QW (policy, SLAs) / M (full coverage) |
| 8.9 Configuration management | Partial | Adopt hardening baselines (CIS benchmarks) for AWS, VMware, OS images, and network devices. Use AWS Config rules and drift detection, and store configs in version control where possible | M |
| 8.10 Information deletion | Gap/Unknown | Retention and deletion schedule, with deletion evidence for cloud storage, backups, and decommissioned VMs. Align with PCI 3.2.1 (limit cardholder data retention) | QW / M |
| 8.11 Data masking | Unknown | Confirm PAN masking and truncation in UIs, logs, and reports (PCI 3.4.1). Define masking for PII in support tools | QW |
| 8.12 Data leakage prevention | Gap | Risk-based. Start with S3 public-access blocks, Macie or equivalent for sensitive data discovery, and email and endpoint controls for CDE-adjacent staff. Full DLP can be justified as phased | M |
| 8.13 Information backup | **Strong** | Add immutability or offline copies (ransomware), cross-account or cross-region copies, and retained restore-test evidence | QW |
| 8.14 Redundancy | Partial | Tie redundancy (multi-AZ, VMware HA) to RTO/RPO from your BIA. Document single points of failure | M |
| 8.15 Logging | Partial/Unknown | Enable CloudTrail in all regions, centralize logs from AWS, VMware, and the CDE, and protect log integrity. Meet PCI 10.5.1 (12 months retention, 3 months immediately available) | M |
| 8.16 Monitoring activities | Gap/Unknown | GuardDuty, alerting rules, and a defined alert-review process. Decide on SIEM or MDR, and whether coverage is 24x7 | M / L |
| 8.17 Clock synchronization | Unknown | Standard NTP source across AWS and on-prem. Required for PCI 10.6 | QW |
| 8.18 Privileged utility programs | Unknown | Inventory and restrict admin tools (hypervisor consoles, DB tools, shell access). Fold into PAM scope | QW |
| 8.19 Software on operational systems | Partial | Approved software list, restricted install rights on servers, and installs routed through change | QW |
| 8.20 Network security; 8.21 Network services | Partial | Likely strong around the CDE due to PCI. Add firewall rule review evidence (PCI 1.2.7, every six months), network diagrams, and a security requirements record for network providers | QW |
| 8.22 Segregation of networks | Partial | CDE segmentation likely exists. Confirm segmentation testing evidence (PCI 11.4.5) and extend the model to production vs. corporate vs. dev | QW / M |
| 8.23 Web filtering | Gap | DNS filtering or a secure web gateway for corporate endpoints | QW / M |
| 8.24 Use of cryptography | Partial | Cryptography policy covering approved algorithms, TLS versions, and key management (AWS KMS, HSM if any), plus key rotation and custodians (PCI 3.6, 3.7, 4.2.1) | QW / M |
| 8.25 Secure development lifecycle; 8.26 Application security requirements; 8.27 Secure architecture; 8.28 Secure coding | Unknown | Applies if you build the payment platform. Document an SDLC, add threat modeling for major changes, set coding standards, and require peer review (PCI 6.2) | M |
| 8.29 Security testing in dev and acceptance | Unknown | SAST, dependency (SCA) scanning, DAST for web apps, annual pen test, and a release gate on critical findings (PCI 6.3, 6.4, 11.4) | M |
| 8.30 Outsourced development | Unknown | Likely N/A if no contractors write code. If you use them, add security clauses and code review requirements | QW |
| 8.31 Separation of dev, test, and prod | Partial | Verify separate AWS accounts or VPCs, separate credentials, and no developer access to production by default (PCI 6.5.3) | QW |
| 8.32 Change management | **Strong** | Your ITIL change process covers most of this. Add a security impact field, an emergency change procedure, and rollback evidence | QW |
| 8.33 Test information | Partial/Unknown | Prohibit live PANs in non-production (PCI 6.5.5). Use synthetic or masked data | QW |
| 8.34 Protection during audit testing | Gap | Short procedure for how pen tests, scans, and auditor access are approved, scoped, and supervised | QW |

## Priority deep-dive: PAM, vulnerability management, access reviews

### 1. Privileged access (8.2, 8.18, 5.18)

| Phase | Actions | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| **Now (weeks 1 to 4)** | Inventory all privileged accounts (AWS root and IAM, domain admin, vCenter, DBs, network, SaaS admin). Enforce MFA on all admin access (PCI 8.4.1). Remove shared and standing admin accounts where possible, and secure and test AWS root and break-glass accounts | QW |
| **Next (months 1 to 3)** | Move AWS admins to IAM Identity Center with least-privilege permission sets and time-bound elevation. Create separate admin accounts for on-prem. Add a documented privileged access request and approval flow in your ITIL tooling. Log privileged activity centrally | QW / M |
| **Later (3 to 9 months)** | Select and deploy a PAM tool with credential vaulting, session recording, and just-in-time access across AWS and VMware. Start with CDE and domain-admin access, then expand | **L** |

For the ISO audit, the interim controls plus a risk-justified PAM roadmap are usually acceptable. Auditors want to see that the risk is understood and being treated, not that every tool is already deployed.

### 2. Vulnerability management (8.8)

| Step | Action | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Write a short vulnerability management standard with severity-based SLAs. A common starting point is critical within 7 to 14 days and high within 30. PCI requires critical patches within one month at minimum | QW |
| 2 | Enable Amazon Inspector for EC2, ECR, and Lambda, and deploy a scanner for on-prem VMware assets. Run authenticated scans | QW / M |
| 3 | Schedule internal scans at least quarterly and after significant change (PCI 11.3.1), plus external ASV scans quarterly (PCI 11.3.2) | QW |
| 4 | Assign every finding an owner (via the CMDB), track it as a ticket, and move patching to **monthly plus out-of-cycle for critical or KEV-listed issues** | M |
| 5 | Add an exception and risk-acceptance process with expiry dates | QW |
| 6 | Report metrics monthly: mean time to remediate, SLA compliance, and aging backlog. Use them as ISMS objectives (Clause 6.2) | QW |

Your current quarterly patching cadence is probably the **single most likely audit finding**, for both ISO and PCI, so it deserves the earliest attention.

### 3. Access reviews (5.15, 5.18, 8.2)

| Step | Action | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reuse the SOX access review process as the base, then extend scope to all in-scope systems: AWS, VMware, CDE apps, databases, and key SaaS | QW |
| 2 | Review standard users at least every six months (PCI 7.2.4) and **privileged users quarterly** | QW |
| 3 | Make reviewers system or data owners, not IT admins reviewing their own access. Record approvals and removals with timestamps | QW |
| 4 | Tie joiner/mover/leaver events to HR triggers, and test that leavers are disabled within your target (for example, 24 hours) | QW / M |
| 5 | Review service accounts, API keys, and IAM roles, which are often missed | M |

## Suggested sequencing

1. **Weeks 1 to 6:** scope, ISMS policy, risk methodology, privileged account inventory and MFA, vulnerability SLAs, scanner enablement, expanded access reviews
2. **Months 2 to 4:** risk assessment and SoA, centralized logging, monthly patching, BIA and DR test, supplier inventory, IR playbooks
3. **Months 4 to 9:** PAM tool, monitoring and detection maturity, SDLC security tooling, internal audit and management review, then Stage 1 and Stage 2 audits

| `[x.x]` | `[Title]` | `[Yes/No]` | `[Reason]` | `[Status]` | `[Evidence]` | `[Owner]` | `[date]` |

**Notes for completing it:**

- **Exclusions need a real reason.** "We don't do that" is weak. "No outsourced development exists in scope, confirmed by [source]" is audit-ready.
- **Don't exclude a control because it's hard.** If the risk assessment says you need it, mark it Planned with a date.
- **Link controls to risks.** Many auditors expect each included control to trace to a risk treatment decision, a legal requirement, or a contractual requirement (such as PCI).
- **Inherited controls** (AWS data centers, colo facilities) should be marked applicable with the provider's attestation as evidence. Review those reports annually.
- Keep PCI and SOX references in the justification column. It shows auditors you're reusing existing evidence, and it saves you from maintaining parallel documents.

# Part 2: Vulnerability Management Standard

**Document ID:** `[SEC-STD-VM-001]` | **Version:** `[0.1]` | **Owner:** ITO | **Approver:** `[CISO/EXEC]` | **Review:** annually
**Maps to:** ISO 27001 A.8.8, 8.9, 5.7 | PCI DSS 6.3.1, 6.3.3, 11.3.1, 11.3.2

## 1. Purpose and scope
This standard defines how vulnerabilities are identified, prioritized, remediated, and reported. It covers all in-scope assets: AWS workloads (EC2, containers, Lambda), on-prem VMware hosts and VMs, network devices, endpoints, and the payment platform's application code and dependencies.

## 2. Roles
- **ITO:** runs scanning and patch cycles, and reports metrics.
- **Asset owners (CLD/ENG/ITO):** remediate findings in their SLA.
- **ISMS:** approves exceptions, reviews metrics, and triages threat intelligence.
- **EXEC:** approves high-risk exceptions.

## 3. Requirements
1. **Asset coverage:** every in-scope asset in the CMDB has an owner and is scanned. Unscanned assets are tracked as findings.
2. **Scanning cadence:**
   - Authenticated internal scans: **at least monthly** (the PCI minimum is quarterly and after significant change).
   - Cloud and container image scanning: continuous or on each build.
   - External ASV scans: quarterly and after significant change.
   - Code and dependency scans (SAST/SCA): on every merge to main.
3. **Prioritization:** rate by CVSS, then adjust for exploitability (CISA KEV, active exploitation), asset criticality (CDE or internet-facing), and compensating controls.
4. **Intelligence:** ISMS reviews CISA KEV and vendor advisories (AWS, VMware, OS, key libraries) at least weekly.
5. **Verification:** closure requires a rescan or other evidence.
6. **Patching:** monthly cycle, plus out-of-cycle for critical, KEV-listed, or actively exploited issues. All patches go through change management.

## 4. Remediation SLAs

| Severity | Standard asset | CDE or internet-facing | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Critical** (or KEV-listed or actively exploited) | 14 days | **7 days** | KEV items: 7 days maximum, with emergency change if needed |
| **High** | 30 days | **14 days** | PCI 6.3.3: no later than one month |
| **Medium** | 60 days | 45 days | |
| **Low** | 90 days or next cycle | 90 days | Track, and fix opportunistically |

- **Clock start:** when the vendor patch is released or the finding is validated, whichever is later.
- **Beyond SLA:** the finding needs an approved exception (see section 5) or it is reported as an SLA breach.
- **Targets:** these SLAs are a starting proposal. Check them against your risk appetite and QSA guidance.

## 5. Exception and risk acceptance process
1. **Request:** the asset owner raises a ticket with the finding ID, asset, business reason, and why the patch can't be applied in SLA.
2. **Compensating controls:** the request must describe them (network isolation, WAF rule, disabled service, added monitoring).
3. **Risk rating:** ISMS assesses residual risk.
4. **Approval:**
   - Medium or Low: ISMS.
   - High: ISMS plus the asset owner's director.
   - Critical, or any CDE asset: EXEC.
5. **Expiry:** maximum 90 days, renewable only with fresh review. No open-ended exceptions.
6. **Register:** all exceptions are logged in a central register and reviewed monthly, with a summary in management review.
7. **PCI note:** exceptions on CDE assets still need to satisfy PCI's patch timeline unless the QSA accepts the compensating controls. Check this with the QSA before approving.

## 6. Metrics and reporting
Report monthly to the ISMS owner, and quarterly in management review:
- % of in-scope assets scanned
- Open findings by severity and age
- SLA compliance %
- Mean time to remediate (by severity)
- Active exceptions and expiry dates
- Count of KEV findings and time to close

Suggested ISMS objectives (Clause 6.2): 95% scan coverage, 90% SLA compliance for Critical and High, zero expired exceptions.

## 7. Records
Scan reports, ticket history, change records, exception register, and monthly metric reports. Retain for `[12 months minimum / per retention schedule]`.

## 8. Compliance
Breaches of this standard are reported to ISMS, and persistent non-compliance is escalated to EXEC.
